subject: Mutual Action Plan — technical evaluation playbook (benchmarks, owners, close target)
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alice Torres <alice.torres@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + draft MAP milestone: technical eval playbook

Hi Alice — great call today, thanks for walking us through the HealthGrid objectives. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the MAP milestone for the technical evaluation. Please correct anything I mis-stated.

Call recap (short):
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for document understanding workload (triage + extraction) at production latencies and cost targets.
- Success = parity on accuracy/QA with your current LLM baseline AND latency/cost within target window (details below).
- Trial scope: 2 week technical evaluation + 4 week pilot if benchmarks pass.

Proposed technical-eval playbook (draft):
1) Test corpus delivery (HealthGrid) — you provide ~10k representative documents + 500 labeled examples. Dependency: test corpus CSV + schema. Owner: HealthGrid (Alice). Target: Aug 24.
2) Benchmarks & acceptance criteria — accuracy: >= baseline F1 - no more than 3 pt drop on core entity set; latency: p95 inference < 120ms for 512-token avg; cost: <$0.20 per 1k generated tokens (est). Owner: Redwood (Rishi) + HealthGrid review. Target: Aug 26.
3) Model shortlist & config — Redwood proposes 3 variants (quantized medium, Llama-3-8B q4f, Redwood-v2-7B opt). Owner: Redwood (Rishi). Target: Aug 21.
4) Trial access & integration — API keys, sample Docker for private network, and test endpoints. Dependency: NDA + trial entitlement. Owner: HealthGrid (procurement) + Redwood infra. Target: Aug 27.
5) Run benchmarks & readout — run end-to-end scripts, produce latency/cost tables and evaluation report. Owner: Redwood (Rishi). Target: Sep 3.
6) Decision gating & pilot kickoff — if benchmarks meet criteria, move to a 4-week pilot; else iterate on model/config. Decision owner: HealthGrid (Alice). Target close (MAP item): Sep 10.

Open asks for you: 1) confirm who will own delivering labeled samples and approximate file format; 2) confirm procurement contact for trial entitlements; 3) confirm we can target Sep 10 as MAP close for the technical milestone.

Attachments: healthgrid-test-corpus.csv (placeholder), draft MAP PDF (attached).

Thanks — I’ll circulate a lightweight MAP doc with the above owners/milestones after I get your confirmation.

Best,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Torres <alice.torres@healthgrid.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthgrid.com, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 12:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + draft MAP milestone: technical eval playbook

Vivek — thanks for the tidy recap. Agree broadly and appreciate the clear owners. Quick responses inline: 

- Labeled samples: we can deliver 500 labeled examples by Aug 25 in CSV (columns: doc_id, text, labels). Owner: me (Alice) but data team will export — cc’d procurement for the NDA.
- Procurement: procurement@healthgrid.com will handle trial paperwork; they need a short SOW and trial duration.
- Model shortlist: happy to see three variants; would prefer a lower-cost quantized run first to validate latency.
- Targets: OK to aim for Sep 10 decision gate, but request a hard readout by Sep 3 so our platform team can prep.

One additional ask: can Redwood include p50/p90/p95 latency breakdown and GPU type used for each run — that will help translate to our infra plan.

I’ll upload the sample export to our secure share once procurement signs the NDA.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Torres
Head of ML, HealthGrid

On Mon, Aug 17, 2026 at 09:12 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> [original message quoted]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alice Torres <alice.torres@healthgrid.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up + draft MAP milestone: technical eval playbook

Hi Alice / Vivek — looping in a slightly more detailed technical proposal and the runbook we plan to use for the 2-week evaluation. Attached: redwood-ma-playbook-draft.pdf (includes scripts, metric calculators, and infra notes). Key points / clarifications: 

1) Model shortlist (initial candidate set):
- RDW-v2-7B-quant (q4f) — expected best cost/latency tradeoff; default for first pass.
- Llama-3-8B-q4 — good accuracy; slightly higher memory, similar latency on A100.
- RDW-v1-13B-onnx — for higher-accuracy comparison if you need recall lift.

2) Benchmarking harness: We will run three seeded evaluation runs per model with your labeled set; compute micro/macro F1, extraction accuracy on core entity set, and robust latency measurements (p50/p90/p95). Scripts will run on A100 and RTX 6000 (we will report GPU type per run).

3) Acceptance thresholds (proposed, editable):
- Accuracy: no more than -3 percentage points vs your baseline F1 on core entities.
- Latency: p95 <= 120ms with batch sizes tuned for 512-token average.
- Cost: raw inference cost < $0.20 per 1k generated tokens across runs (ex post calculated).

4) Dependencies / blockers:
- Labeled set + schema delivered on or before Aug 25.
- Trial API access + any IP whitelisting for HealthGrid IPs.
- Procurement-signed trial SOW and NDA for private endpoints (if using VPC).

5) Ownership matrix (short):
- Data delivery: HealthGrid (Alice)
- Trial entitlement & SOW: HealthGrid procurement
- Run execution & reporting: Redwood (Rishi)
- Model config & tuning: Redwood research team (cc Lauren)
- Final decision/go-live: HealthGrid execs

Next steps I propose: Vivek will post the MAP doc in Drive; Alice / procurement confirm NDA path; we receive sample CSV; Rishi schedules first run (ETA Aug 28 if data arrives on time).

Attachments referenced: redwood-ma-playbook-draft.pdf (contains command examples, eval script names, and expected output CSVs).

Let me know if you want us to add more conservative latency targets for specific GPU classes.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Torres <alice.torres@healthgrid.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthgrid.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up + draft MAP milestone: technical eval playbook

Thanks Rishi — that level of detail helps. Procurement, please see the requested SOW/term outline below and advise on timeline for the NDA so we can share the labeled set by Aug 25.

Vivek — we confirm the owners you listed. We prefer Redwood to run quantized candidate first and provide p50/p90/p95 + GPU type. Sep 3 readout and Sep 10 decision gate are OK.

I’ll upload a small sample CSV today to the Drive link and loop procurement for the SOW.

Best,
Alice

Head of ML, HealthGrid
